Method note: I did not count the sensitivity-only alternative-prior additions (T:p18-b2; T:p22-b3) or the p_unb>=0.2 marginal group (T:p7-b6), because the final retained candidate samples are the four 6-D objects not assigned >99% bound-outlier probability (T:p16-b8) and the 19 Table 3 stars (T:p22-b1).

Gaia DR2 5932173855446728064: At T:p17-b2 the bullet labels 747±3 km/s as v_r, but Table 2 (T:p23-b0) reports 747±3 km/s as the total Galactocentric speed v_g and -728.7±2.5 km/s as v_r,g; Table 1 (T:p8-b0) gives the heliocentric rv as -614.29±2.49 km/s. I therefore treated 747±3 km/s as galactic_rest_frame_velocity and retained the Table 1 heliocentric radial velocity. The paper's p_b = 0 at T:p16-b7 is a bound-outlier likelihood, not a bound probability, so it was not recorded as bound_probability.

Gaia DR2 1383279090527227264: At T:p17-b3, the sentence "At a distance of 10.0 ± 0.9 kpc..." matches Table 2's galactocentric radius r_g = 10.0 ± 0.9 kpc rather than the heliocentric distance d_h = 8.5 ± 1.3 kpc; the 10.0 ± 0.9 kpc value is therefore recorded only as galactocentric_radius. The paper reports an unbound probability (p_unb = 1.00), not a bound probability; no bound_probability value is derived here.

Gaia DR2 1478837543019912064: Target is Gaia DR2 1478837543019912064. The text reports p_b = 0.86, described as the chance that the star is not just a bound-population outlier (T:p16-b8); this is not the same as a bound probability and is not extracted as bound_probability. Table 2's v_r,g = -171.3 ± 1.5 km/s (T:p23-b0) is a Solar-motion-corrected Galactic-frame radial component, not the heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, so only the Table 1 Gaia rv is recorded as radial_velocity. No explicit bound_probability is reported for this star.

Gaia DR2 6456587609813249536: Table 2 lists p_unb=0.98 for the target. Section 3.3 separately reports a 49% chance of being unbound given the pool of other sources (N_b=0.98); this is a distinct bound-outlier statistic and is retained with that condition. The Galactic-frame radial velocity v_r,g=-82.0±2.8 km/s in Table 2 is not used as the radial_velocity quantity because the requested radial velocity excludes Galactic-rest-frame values.

Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376: Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376 appears only in Table 3 (T:p23-b1), the 5-D sample selected by tangential speed without radial velocity. Table 3 provides Galactic coordinates (l,b), not equatorial RA/Dec, and gives no parallax, proper motion, or radial velocity. Its v_t,g = 917.2±107.1 km/s is tangential speed only, not total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The reported p_unb = 1.00 is recorded as unbound_probability; bound probability is not explicitly reported and is not calculated.

Gaia DR2 1240475894700468736: Gaia DR2 1240475894700468736 appears only in Table 3, the 5-D sample selected by tangential speed without radial velocities. The table gives Galactic coordinates (l,b), not equatorial RA/Dec; it does not list parallax or proper motion, and it reports only the tangential Galactic-frame speed v_t,g rather than the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed. The tabulated p_unb is the unbound probability from tangential velocity and astrometric uncertainties; no bound probability is explicitly reported.

Gaia DR2 1570348658847157888: The target appears only in Table 3 (T:p23-b1 / I:p23-b1), the 5-D tangential-speed-selected sample without radial velocities; it is not in Tables 1 or 2. No equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, or radial velocity are reported for it, so those quantities are not extracted. Its listed v_t,g = 885.7 ± 179.0 km/s is a tangential speed, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity.

Gaia DR2 1312242152517660800: The target appears only in Table 3, the 5-D sample without radial velocity. The table reports tangential Galactic rest-frame speed v_t,g = 837.0 ± 172.1 km/s, but not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so no galactic_rest_frame_velocity value is recorded. The paper does not report right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, or radial velocity for this target in the supplied material.

Gaia DR2 4727516205455716224: The target appears in Table 3, the 5-D tangential-speed sample selected without radial velocities. The reported speed in Table 3 is v_t,g, the tangential component, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Gaia DR2 1820299950021811072: The target star Gaia DR2 1820299950021811072 appears only in Table 3 (the 5-D, proper-motion-only sample), so no equatorial coordinates (ra/dec) or radial velocity are reported for it; only Galactic coordinates (l,b) = (54.89, -6.08) deg are given. The listed v_t,g = 877.3 ± 208.9 km/s is a tangential speed, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Text on p22 (T:p22-b1) notes this star is among the most significantly reddened sources (E(B-V) = 0.287 from IRSA). Table 3 values are computed with d_h = 1/parallax; the Bayesian prior analyses (T:p22-b3) change the sample but no individual revised values are given for this star.
